t: Prussia held roughly three fifths of Germany's territory and population and became a parliamentary democracy under its constitution of 30 November 1920.
Under Minister President Otto Braun and Interior Minister Carl Severing it was considered a bulwark of democracy within the Weimar Republic.
Franz von Papen's Prussian coup d'état of July 1932 removed its government; under Hermann Göring it served the Nazi regime until the Allied Control Council abolished it on 25 February 1947.
dyk: The Gestapo grew out of the Prussian political police, which came under Hermann Göring after Hitler named him Reich commissioner of the Interior for Prussia in 1933.
ev: On 12 November representatives of the Berlin workers' and soldiers' councils declare the previous Prussian government deposed
The Prussian State Assembly is elected on 26 January and the Weimar Coalition forms a government in March
The Kapp Putsch collapses after six days; Otto Braun becomes minister president and the constitution is adopted on 30 November
French and Belgian troops occupy the Ruhr, and a Rhenish Republic survives less than a month
Blood May costs 33 lives in Berlin, and the Prussian Concordat with the Vatican is signed on 14 June
After the Altona Bloody Sunday, Hindenburg appoints Papen Reich commissioner for Prussia on 20 July
Göring becomes Prussian minister president, and the Landtag meets for the last time on 18 May
Control Council Law No. 46 of 25 February decrees the dissolution of Prussia

f.founder: The revolutionary government of the MSPD and USPD under Paul Hirsch, November 1918
f.successor: Divided among Poland, the Soviet Union and the post-war German states
